2541c1b5b7.q: What is the star 72 code scam and how do fraudsters use it to intercept bank calls?
2541c1b5b7.a: Star 72 followed by a 10-digit number (area code, exchange, and last four digits of a phone number) is a fraudster's technique to forward all incoming calls to their own phone number. This allows them to intercept legitimate bank or credit union calls, impersonate the financial institution, and authorize fraudulent transactions like cashing fake checks. Star 73 reverses this call forwarding setup.

ad90e173e9.q: How do fraudsters use one-time PIN codes to gain access to bank accounts during phone scams?
ad90e173e9.a: Fraudsters pose as bank or credit union employees and convince victims their accounts are at risk. They obtain the victim's username and password, then claim they will send a one-time PIN to verify identity. Because the victim believes they are speaking with a legitimate institution employee, they provide the PIN when prompted, giving the fraudster complete access to the account.

66280f951c.q: What is the most effective defense against fraudsters impersonating your bank on the phone?
66280f951c.a: The most effective defense is to tell the caller you will call them back, then hang up and dial the official number of your bank or credit union that you know and trust. This stops fraudsters because they will give fake phone numbers. Additionally, legitimate financial institutions will never ask you for your one-time PIN if they call you—only if you call them.
